reaction.episode: The current episode is DIGESTION through the Oct 26 close (data fresh, not stale): SPX closed at 7676.77, 2.14% below its 120-day high, 0.27% below its 50-day and 5.23% above its 200-day; SMH occupies Zone 1 at 541.62, 19.38% off its high, while NVDA at 216 sits just above its Zone 1; VIX is 18.39 and HY OAS 3.23% with credit calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is 2 of 4.
reaction.invalidation: A held close above the SPX 7750–7820 / SMH 580–600 failure zone proves the Watch stance too cautious and voids the ladder's downside rungs, while HY OAS above 4% or a VIX spike above 25 proves the rotation read wrong and voids the ladder's upside rungs.

ladder.response: Stage the Tranche A probe against the deployment ladder's conditions; size only on confirmation prints, never on the zone print alone
ladder.trigger: SMH closes into Zone 2 (470–505) or NVDA into its Zone 2 (175–185)

ladder.response: Treat as the trap case: no chasing the first bounce, no adding into the failure zone; wait for the second low to form and hold
ladder.trigger: Bounce carries SMH into 580–600 or SPX into 7750–7820, then closes back below the zone

ladder.response: Stand down: the rotation read breaks, the ladder voids, and no new risk is staged until credit and trend stabilize
ladder.trigger: HY OAS above 4% or VIX above 25, or SPX closes below its 200-day (7295.09)

ladder.response: Digestion over: re-engage staged adds, starting with the DATA_AHEAD names whose revenue growth already confirmed (AVGO, CLS, LRCX)
ladder.trigger: Held close above SPX 7750–7820 and SMH above 580–600

ladder.response: Do not average down into the fall; the next staging ground is Zone 2, and entries wait for the capitulation tally to confirm
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below 540 on expanding volume without a volume climax reversal

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the base risk of this episode: the tally is only 2 of 4 with no VIX rollover and no volume climax, and Monday's tape already shows the trap shape (TSLT +12.53% in a day, VRT +5.14%) inside an unresolved digestion. Entries therefore require either a confirmed second low that holds or a held break above the failure zone; the first bounce is evidence to watch, never a signal to buy.

strategyPosture: Watch and stage, not chase. The episode is digestion with the AI complex inside Zone 1 but only 2 of 4 capitulation signals confirmed and the FOMC decision one session away, so the work today is holding staged triggers, not adding on Monday's bounce.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real even if the rollover is not confirmed: GOOGL, the weakest Mag 7 name, is 22.5% off its high while AAPL is only 2.2% off. Rotation means the damage is concentrated in the names that carried the index, so index-level calm understates single-name risk in the book.
themes.dataAnchor: The concentration read is ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER: Mag 7 names average 13.37% below their 52-week highs against SPY only 2.1% below its high, an 11.27-point divergence gap, while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold). SPY itself is down just 0.38% over the month and closed Monday up 1.11%. The index is holding while leadership churns, and credit is not confirming a rollover.
themes.label: Leadership rotation, not a broad rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads like an AI unwind: the Mag 7 sit far below their highs and the month's laggard board is crowded with former leaders, which invites a broad-risk-off read.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or lending standards tightening would flip this from rotation to rollover.

themes.counterRead: Washed-out is not the same as bottomed. The mechanical capitulation tally is only 2 of 4: zone occupancy and credit calm confirm, but there is no volume climax reversal and no VIX rollover yet. These are watch-and-stage names, not chase-the-bounce names, and the multiple-compression cases (AMAT, KLAC, ANET) need valuation work, not just a revenue print.
themes.dataAnchor: The revenue data runs the other way. AVGO, a holding, is 33.5% below its high while revenue grows 55% YoY with a 67.8% gross margin, and it carries the top conviction score (82, tier A). CLS is 48% off its high on 66.8% revenue growth, LRCX 45.8% off on 131.3% growth, ONTO 47.3% off on 22.1% growth, and VRT, a holding, 47.4% off on 27.7% growth. SMH sits inside Zone 1 (540–565) at 541.62, and NVDA at 216 sits just above its Zone 1 (200–210).
themes.label: AI/semiconductor washout: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The AI complex is being priced as if the buildout story broke: SMH is 19.38% off its 120-day high and the dislocation list runs 31 names deep, most of them semis, power, and AI suppliers.
themes.watchFor: SMH holding the 540 Zone 1 floor on a closing basis, or printing into Zone 2 (470–505), decides whether this washout stages or deepens.

themes.counterRead: Alignment cuts both ways tomorrow: a decision that pushes the 10-year through 5% on a hawkish surprise, or a dovish surprise that ignites the first bounce, both resolve the digestion in one session. The 10-year level, not the headline, is the tradable signal.
themes.dataAnchor: The 10-year stands at 4.99% against a 2-year of 4.77%, a 2s10s curve of +0.22, a real 10-year of 2.64%, and HY OAS of 3.23% — calm credit, a mildly positive curve, no stress signal. The FOMC Oct 27–28 event carries HIGH signal strength with 9 headline hits, and the Sep CPI event (Oct 14) remains active. Rates and equities agree on the current state: digestion, not distress.
themes.label: FOMC eve with the 10-year pinned under 5%
themes.narrative: With the FOMC decision landing tomorrow (Oct 28), the market is positioned for a rates verdict, and the 10-year hovering just under 5% is the number everyone is watching.
themes.watchFor: The 10-year closing above 5.00% or below 4.80% in the 48 hours after the decision.

themes.counterRead: TSLT's single-day 12.53% snap is a warning, not a vindication: leveraged names move hardest in both directions during digestion, and a one-day spike inside an unresolved episode is exactly how entries get trapped. Judge the split on closes across the week, not on Monday's bounce.
themes.dataAnchor: Over the month, BMNR is down 23.48% and fell a further 5.85% on Monday, CONL is down 34.39%, META is down 16.35% and NFLX 10.60%, while TSLT leads the month up 10.34% and jumped 12.53% on Monday, MA is up 7.84% on the month, and VST is up 3.69% with VRT rebounding 5.14% on Monday despite a 19.34% monthly decline. The drawdown lives in leveraged and treasury-beta exposure; the compounders and the power name are absorbing it.
themes.label: Book split: leveraged beta bleeds, quality compounders hold
themes.narrative: A quick glance at SPY's flat month suggests the book should be flat too, but the holdings are splitting hard along a leverage-and-quality line.
themes.watchFor: BMNR and CONL stabilizing on closes rather than single-day snaps, and VRT holding its Monday rebound into the week.

watchFor: SMH closing below 540 (Zone 1 floor breaks, Zone 2 staging begins) or above 580 (failure-zone retest starts)
FOMC decision Oct 28 and the 10-year closing above 5.00% or below 4.80% in the following 48 hours
HY OAS breaking above 4% or VIX above 25 (stand-down / regime-break)
SPX held close above 7750–7820 (digestion over, re-entry condition)
Mechanical capitulation tally moving from 2 of 4 toward confirmation (volume climax reversal or VIX rollover printing)
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in the AI complex around the SMH Zone 1 floor (540) and the failure zone above (580–600): either the floor holds and the FOMC verdict starts the retest, or the floor gives way and Zone 2 (470–505) becomes the staging ground.
